sections.content: How many people stayed in Platt Bridge after gaining qualifications?

Platt Bridge is a small town in the North West. Platt Bridge does not have its own university.

Platt Bridge has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Platt Bridge ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 450 state-school pupils from Platt Bridge who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 80 (18%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 155 (34%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Platt Bridge to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Platt Bridge's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Platt Bridge in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

In 2018 to 2019, 47% of graduates and 40% of qualified non-graduates living in Platt Bridge had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 95 graduates and 175 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Platt Bridge. This is compared with the 80 graduates and 155 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 53% of the graduates had also lived in Platt Bridge as GCSE pupils, while 47% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Platt Bridge in 2018 to 2019, 60% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 40% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
